m.n: The Holy Trinity & The Nicene Creed

co.n: The Holy Trinity & The Nicene Creed Cohort

c.p: How does Catholic dogma define the mystery of the Most Holy Trinity?
c.a: one god in three distinct divine persons: father, son, and holy spirit | one god in three divine persons | three persons in one god
c.h: The three Persons share the exact same single divine essence, yet are distinct in their eternal relations.
c.e: The Trinity is One: Catholics worship one God in three Persons—the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit—co-equal, co-eternal, and consubstantial (CCC 253–256).
r: three separate gods who hold committee meetings
This is the heresy of polytheism or tritheism; Catholic monotheism affirms strictly One God in three divine Persons.
one god wearing three different costumes different times
This is the heresy of modalism; the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit are truly distinct Persons simultaneously, not temporary masks.

c.p: What does the word "consubstantial" (homoousios) in the Nicene Creed affirm about the Son and the Father?
c.a: the son is of the exact same divine substance and nature as the father | of the same substance as the father | same nature as the father
c.h: Proclaimed at the Council of Nicaea (325 AD) to reject the Arian heresy.
c.e: Consubstantial affirms that Jesus Christ is not a created being, but true God from true God, possessing the identical divine nature as God the Father (CCC 242, 465).
r: that the son was the first creature made god
The Creed explicitly denies this by declaring Christ is "begotten, not made, consubstantial with the Father".
